subject: ggmap + multiple geom_polygon, problem in getting any (decent) legend

messages.author: 52137764689f2117
messages.subject: ggmap + multiple geom_polygon, problem in getting any (decent) legend
parts:
Hi all,

I managed to create some nice maps, with on top of them countries coloured according to some values, using multiple geom_polygon additions, but then I fail to make any legend visible. Any help is much appreciated.
Here is the code (bit simplified, but it will do):

library(RColorBrewer);
library(rgdal);
library(ggmap);
library(rgeos);
library(maptools);
library(countrycode);

colorSelector <- function(value, minv, maxv) {
  colorPalette <- brewer.pal(9, "Reds");
  return(colorPalette[min(9, max(1, (9 - (8*(maxv - value)/(maxv - minv))), na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)]);
}

EU_W__mapC <- get_map(location = 'europe', zoom=4, maptype = 'hybrid');
eurMap <- readOGR(dsn = paste0(RDir,"ShapeFiles EU"), layer="TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3"); # this data set is publicly available from http://thematicmapping.org/downloads/world_borders.php
eurMap <- spTransform(eurMap, CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84"));

#gatheredDataIn is an 2D-array containing some data (number of persons per country involved to be exact, with column names being the full country names and row names different years)
CountryFullNames <- colnames(gatheredDataIn); 
CountryCodeNames <- countrycode(sourcevar = CountryFullNames, origin = 'country.name', destination = 'iso2c');

fullPicture <- ggmap(EU_W__mapC);
dataValues = unlist(gatheredDataIn[1, ]);

for (c in 1:length(CountryCodeNames)) {
  if(!is.na(dataValues[c]) && sum(eurMap$ISO2 == CountryCodeNames[c]) > 0) {
    polygonData <- (eurMap[eurMap$ISO2 == CountryCodeNames[c], ]);
    polygonDataF = fortify(polygonData);
    colorSel <- colorSelector(dataValues[c], min(dataValues, na.rm = TRUE), max(dataValues, na.rm = TRUE));
    fullPicture <- fullPicture + geom_polygon(data = polygonDataF, aes(x = long, y = lat, group=group), colour = colorSel, fill = colorSel, alpha=0.6, size = 0);
# adding 
#     geom_polygon(data = polygonDataF, aes(x = long, y = lat, group=group, color=group, shape=group), alpha=0.6, size = 0); 
# instead creates a data-variable for which he fails to plot anything. R just crashes after several minutes
    remove(polygonData);
    remove(polygonDataF);
  }
}

typing fullPicture at the console prompt plots then a very nice map, as desired, with the countries colored according to the values of dataValues, but no legend visible, no matter what explicit command I add (theme_bw(), guide_legend(), ...). See also attachment.


Any help is welcome,
Best,
Patrick

parts:
Hi all,

Thanks to Dennis Murphy I find meanwhile the solution. 
BTW, RDir is just a variable containing the path where all my data is stored.

So here comes the correct solution for getting it nice and clean within seconds (code is a bit cleaned with respect to the previous one):

library(RColorBrewer);
library(rgdal);
library(ggmap);
library(rgeos);
library(maptools);
library(countrycode);

colorSelector <- function(value, minv, maxv) {
  colorPalette <- brewer.pal(9, "Reds");
  return(colorPalette[min(9, max(1, (9 - (8*(maxv - value)/(maxv - minv))), na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE)]);
}

EU_W__mapC <- get_map(location = 'europe', zoom=4, maptype = 'hybrid');
eurMap <- readOGR(dsn = paste0(RDir,"ShapeFiles EU"), layer="TM_WORLD_BORDERS-0.3"); # this data set is publicly available from http://thematicmapping.org/downloads/world_borders.php
eurMap <- spTransform(eurMap, CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84"));

#gatheredDataIn is an 2D-array containing some data (number of persons per country involved to be exact, with column names being the full country names and row names different years)
CountryFullNames <- colnames(gatheredDataIn); 
CountryCodeNames <- countrycode(sourcevar = CountryFullNames, origin = 'country.name', destination = 'iso2c');

fullPicture <- ggmap(EU_W__mapC);
dataValues = unlist(gatheredDataIn[1, ]);

maxv = max(dataValues, na.rm = TRUE);
minv = min(dataValues, na.rm = TRUE);
if(!is.na(dataValues[c]) && !is.na(CountryCodeNames[c]) && sum(eurMap$ISO2 == CountryCodeNames[c]) > 0) {

polygonData <- (eurMap[eurMap$ISO2 == CountryCodeNames[c], ]);
    polygonDataF = fortify(polygonData);

colorSel <- colorSelector(dataValues[c], minv, maxv);
    polygonDataF$id = colorSel;
    fullPicture <- fullPicture + 
      geom_polygon(data = polygonDataF, aes(x = long, y = lat, group=group, colour = id, fill = id), alpha=0.4, size = 0);
    remove(polygonData);
    remove(polygonDataF);
  }
}

fullPictureL <- fullPicture + ggtitle("# Persons involve");
fullPictureL <- fullPictureL + 
   scale_fill_discrete(name = "# Persons", breaks=brewer.pal(9, "Reds"), labels = round(seq(from=minv, to=maxv, length.out=9), digits = 0)) +
   scale_color_discrete(name = "# Persons", breaks=brewer.pal(9, "Reds"), labels = round(seq(from=minv, to=maxv, length.out=9), digits = 0)) +
   theme(axis.ticks = element_blank(),
         axis.text.x = element_blank(),
         axis.text.y = element_blank(),
         axis.title.x = element_blank(),
         axis.title.y = element_blank());
fullPictureL

Note that since both colour and fill are set within the aes environment, you need to adapt both colour and fill (through scale_color_discrete and scale_fill_discrete, respectively) to get a single correct legend.
If you forget one of both commands, you will end up with two scales/legends. Took some while to figure that out, but finally, the result is there (see attach).

Best,
Patrick
